item.title: Department stores gain 8.43% share as Shein drops 0.37pp ahead of Golden Quarter
item.description:
John Lewis, Harrods and Selfridges together accounted for 8.43% of UK fashion and retail searches between July and September 2026. Meanwhile, Shein’s search share fell 0.37 percentage points year on year, the largest drop among online‑first retailers.
Next led the pack with a 7.16% share of fashion brand searches, followed by Primark at 5.82%, Sports Direct at 4.17%, TK Maxx at 3.82% and Vinted at 3.54%, all showing year‑on‑year growth. Overall brand search demand softened during the quarter, yet shoppers continued to favour value‑oriented and second‑hand retailers over full‑price premium brands. MediaVision’s analysis shows that retailers able to span multiple categories, occasions and price points are entering the festive period with momentum.
“While the wider fashion market has experienced a seasonal slowdown, established names including John Lewis, Harrods and Selfridges have all strengthened their share of brand demand,” Louis Venter, CEO of MediaVision said.
Prior to the Golden Quarter, overall brand search demand had softened across the wider market. Next’s strong Q2 performance helped it retain the top share of fashion brand searches.
Source: InternetRetailing (https://internetretailing.net/department-stores-gain-ground-as-digital-only-fashion-retailers-lose-share-ahead-of-golden-quarter)

item.title: AI-driven expectations push 45% of UK shoppers toward returns
item.description:
The MACH Alliance reported that 45% of UK shoppers say unrealistic AI-driven expectations would make them more likely to return a product. A majority of shoppers (56%) believe AI exaggerates what products will look like or do before they buy.
Over two-thirds of respondents (68%) said AI-generated product images often look too perfect to match the real item. In social commerce, AI directly influences 45% of spending. The same poll found that 41% of ecommerce purchases are shaped by AI agents.
“Connected ecosystems are how retailers close the AI expectations gap. When agents, data and best-of-breed technologies work together, what shoppers see during discovery is much closer to what arrives at their door,” Jason Cottrell, President of the MACH Alliance said.
The MACH Alliance, a global vendor-neutral body that sets standards for composable enterprise technology, surveyed over 1,000 UK shoppers about AI’s role in buying. It noted that without a connected tech ecosystem, retailers using AI to boost front-end conversions risk creating unrealistic expectations that lead to returns.
Source: ChannelX (https://channelx.world/2026/10/inflated-ai-product-expectations-risk-45-of-uk-shoppers-making-returns)

item.title: Lenskart shares drop up to 5% intraday as Alpha Wave signals stake sale
item.description:
Lenskart’s shares slipped as much as 5% intraday on the BSE today after Alpha Wave Ventures signaled a possible stake sale. The investor is looking to offload up to 1.6% of its holding for as much as ₹1,691 crore, pricing the floor at ₹640 per share.
Lenskart’s market capitalisation stood at ₹1,13,098.38 crore at the time of the dip. The proposed sale involves 15.1 million shares (about 0.9% of the company) with an option to sell another 11.3 million shares (roughly 0.7%). If the full 26.4 million shares are sold, Alpha Wave’s stake would fall from 3.42% to 1.82%. In August, the fund sold 2.94 crore shares at ₹630 each, fetching ₹1,856.8 crore, and earlier this year SoftBank, Temasek and the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority also offloaded sizable blocks.
SoftBank sold Lenskart shares worth ₹2,887.9 crore, while Temasek offloaded a 2.05% stake for ₹1,934 crore last month. Earlier, in June, Abu Dhabi Investment Authority sold 4 crore Lenskart shares in a block deal worth ₹1,960 crore.
Source: Inc42 (https://inc42.com/buzz/lenskart-shares-slump-5-amid-bulk-deal-buzz)

item.title: Survey Shows Two-Thirds of Firms Have Evaluated Payment Guarantees
item.description:
A survey of 150 senior payment and finance executives found that two-thirds of firms have evaluated or used a payment guarantee, while only 13% currently use one. The same survey shows 95% of executives anticipate at least some benefit from payment guarantees, with none foreseeing a downside.
The research was conducted to understand the barriers preventing wider use of payment guarantees. It gathered insights from senior executives responsible for payments and finance. The goal was to identify where guarantees could add value beyond simple loss coverage. Participants were asked about their expectations and current practices. The results highlight a mismatch between perceived benefits and actual adoption rates. Many firms see guarantees as a way to streamline risk management. Others emphasize the potential to improve customer confidence in payments. A smaller group points to cost savings in reconciliation work. The study also notes that confidence in existing fraud systems can obscure real‑time weaknesses. Firms with more sophisticated fraud monitoring tend to be more open to trying guarantees. Overall, the findings suggest a need for better education and clearer value propositions. Stakeholders may use this information to guide future investments. By addressing the adoption gap, businesses could experience smoother cash flows and lower operational strain. Such improvements may also strengthen relationships with customers and suppliers. The survey also highlights that clear communication about guarantee terms could encourage greater uptake.
Source: PYMNTS (https://pymnts.com/news/b2b-payments/2026/more-than-two-thirds-of-firms-lose-or-delay-revenue-when-payments-fail)

item.title: AI agents promise $236 billion market opportunity for small businesses by 2034
item.description:
AI agents are giving small businesses operational capacity that previously required hiring, as the global AI agents market is projected to reach $236 billion by 2034. An OECD report finds that agentic AI is a particular opportunity for small businesses lacking internal AI teams, mapping SME AI maturity across four levels from novice to champion.
A World Economic Forum article estimates that agentic AI could generate $3 trillion in corporate productivity gains globally over the next decade. The article also notes that a know-your-agent framework, built on top of know-your-customer standards, is needed for small businesses to participate safely in the agent economy. Klarna managed a large portion of customer service interactions through autonomous agents while keeping escalation paths for complex cases.
Running a small business has always meant doing more with less. The owner takes the morning shift, answers customer emails on lunch, reconciles the books at night and handles scheduling on weekends.
Source: PYMNTS (https://pymnts.com/news/artificial-intelligence/2026/ai-agents-give-main-street-businesses-big-business-muscle)

item.title: More Than Half of Card Switchers Choose an Existing Card, PYMNTS Reports
item.description:
PYMNTS Intelligence found that 58% of U.S. consumers who switched their primary credit card in the past two years elevated a card they already had. That shift represents roughly 45 million switchers moving an existing card into the top of wallet position, compared with 33 million who opted for a newly issued card.
The findings come from a PYMNTS Intelligence survey conducted in June 2024 of 2,460 U.S. adults holding at least one general‑purpose credit card, of which 884 had changed their primary card in the previous 24 months. Among those switchers, 71% settled on their new primary card within a month, with 17% deciding in less than a week and another 29% taking one to two weeks. Forty‑six percent reported no contact with their former issuer before making the switch, while only 17% said the issuer reached out and those contacts typically lacked a meaningful offer. Looking ahead, 29% of recent switchers say they are very or extremely likely to change their primary card again in the next year, compared with just 5% of consumers who have not switched. When issuers did make a retention attempt, the most common offers were annual‑fee relief at 32%, statement credits or cash back at 31%, promises to improve the digital experience at 31%, and bonus points or miles at 31%.
Issuers often assume their biggest retention threat is a rival bank winning a new‑account application. The PYMNTS report, produced in collaboration with Elan, shows that the threat frequently comes from cards already present in the consumer’s wallet.
Source: PYMNTS (https://pymnts.com/credit-cards/2026/71-percent-of-card-switchers-choose-a-card-already-in-their-wallet)

item.title: ASOS confirms cyber breach exposing names and contacts, shares drop 11%
item.description:
On 6 October 2026, ASOS said a hacking incident accessed basic personal information such as names and contact details, and its shares fell 11% in morning trading. The retailer said an unauthorised party gained access to an employee account, prompting an immediate lockdown and investigation.
ASOS locked down the affected platforms and launched a full investigation with internal and external cyber experts.
“What makes the ASOS incident so damaging is that it came through the push notifications customers had chosen to receive,” Marty Bauer, ecommerce expert at Omnisend said.
“This is the cyber equivalent of hijacking a shop’s Tannoy and announcing a breach to every customer in the store,” Jonathan Lee, director of cyber strategy at TrendAI said.
Source: Retail Gazette (https://retailgazette.co.uk/blog/2026/10/asos-cyber-incident-industry-reacts)

item.title: Tesco puts influencer content on 3,800 in-store screens
item.description:
Tesco announced at its Tesco Media Upfront event last week that it will place influencer-led videos across its network of more than 3,800 digital screens, including 2,800 in Tesco Express stores. Tesco Media said 40 per cent of shoppers under 45 actively follow influencers for brand and product recommendations, offering advertisers a route to turn online inspiration into in‑store purchases.
The influencer-led videos will appear on Tesco’s website, mobile app, and across its network of more than 3,800 digital screens, including 2,800 located in Tesco Express stores. Tesco has partnered with Kevel to launch Ad Manager, a self‑service platform that uses AI‑powered tools and Clubcard data to help brands plan, book, measure, and optimise campaigns. Advertisers can use Ad Manager to target existing Clubcard holders or potential new buyers, with the system providing audience‑reach forecasts before a campaign goes live.
“It’s about better technology and, crucially, the ability to use it dynamically rather than posting one static message,” Simon Lonsdale, Tesco Media partnerships and digital growth director said.
“Because only one in four products are bought out of habit, there’s a huge opportunity to influence behaviour,” Steve Edwards, Tesco Media head of agency said.
Influencer-led campaigns are already being tested, with content set to appear across Tesco’s website, app, and in-store screens. Tesco is also introducing video advertising into its online shopping experience as part of its wider push to expand its retail media business.
Source: Retail Gazette (https://retailgazette.co.uk/blog/2026/10/tesco-to-bring-influencer-content-into-stores-in-retail-media-shake-up)

item.title: Morrisons launches fourth robot delivery trial in Cambourne as Just Eat expands
item.description:
On 11 October 2026, Morrisons launched its fourth autonomous delivery robot trial in Cambourne, marking Just Eat's expansion of the service to a new area. The trial adds delivery capacity ahead of the festive season and during regular Half Price Wednesdays promotions on Just Eat.
Shoppers ordering from the Cambourne Morrisons store via the Just Eat app will have their orders delivered exclusively by robot. Three existing Morrisons Daily stores in Sunderland and Milton Keynes already use the same robot delivery service. The robots, operated by Starship Technologies, navigate pavements and crossings to deliver groceries directly to customers' doors. No additional fee is charged for the robot delivery option, which is presented as a standard delivery choice at checkout.
“We are pleased to be working with Just Eat and Starship Technologies to trial autonomous robot deliveries from our Cambourne supermarket as we continue exploring innovative ways to serve our local community,” Charlotte Exell, Group Online Director at Morrisons said.
This is the first trial location where it doesn't already offer grocery delivery and builds on Sunderland and Milton Keynes deployments. In addition to Cambourne, the trial is also underway across three of our Morrisons Daily stores.
Source: Retail Technology Innovation Hub (https://retailtechinnovationhub.com/home/2026/10/11/morrisons-becomes-one-of-first-uk-grocery-brands-to-tap-autonomous-delivery-as-just-eat-expands-trial)

item.title: THG Commerce adds Criteo Sponsored Products to AI Shopping Assistant
item.description:
On 11 October 2026, THG Commerce integrated Criteo Sponsored Products into its AI Shopping Assistant built on Google Cloud’s Gemini Enterprise. Early results show sponsored products surfaced through the AI Shopping Assistant achieved a click‑through rate more than five times the average and a conversion rate more than double the average.
The AI Shopping Assistant extracts keywords and filters from each conversation and turns them into tailored product recommendations, showing sponsored products only when they match the shopper’s query. Sponsored recommendations appear clearly labelled alongside organic suggestions within the same conversational response, using Criteo’s existing relevance models that apply keyword matching, semantic understanding and strict relevance thresholds. The service is delivered as a plug‑and‑play SaaS offering via Google Cloud Marketplace and can operate independently of any underlying storefront, alongside THG Commerce’s AI Stylist and Shopping Assistant Insights.
“By bringing Criteo Sponsored Products into our AI Shopping Assistant, we're helping retailers monetise those moments using the infrastructure they already have, while making sure every sponsored recommendation is relevant to what the shopper asked for,” Darren Rajanah, Chief Revenue Officer, THG Ingenuity said.
“By bringing Criteo Sponsored Products into THG Commerce’s AI Shopping Assistant, brands can engage shoppers in high intent moments with relevant, clearly labelled recommendations, while retailers retain control of the experience,” Andy Stephen, Managing Director Retail Media UK, Criteo said.
The integration builds on THG Ingenuity’s existing partnership with Criteo and its broader collaboration with Google Cloud. THG Commerce has previously launched agentic commerce solutions on Gemini Enterprise, including the AI Stylist for virtual try‑on and Shopping Assistant Insights for shopper analytics.
Source: Retail Technology Innovation Hub (https://retailtechinnovationhub.com/home/2026/10/11/first-for-thg-commerce-as-it-brings-criteo-sponsored-products-to-ai-shopping-assistant-solution)

item.title: Receivers table two formal offers for Cue Clothing Co
item.description:
Receivers FTI Consulting tabled two formal offers for Cue Clothing Co almost one month after the retailer entered administration and receivership. The offers come from Larry Kestelman’s Brand Collective and Justin Levis, son of founder Rod Levis.
At the start of the receivership process, Cue lost five stores from its network. FTI Consulting continues to meet with creditors and manage interest in the business. Brand Collective recently acquired Glue Store, The Dom and Running Bare, describing the move as a “significant step forward”.
“difficult decision,” FTI Consulting, Receiver said.
“These acquisitions demonstrate Brand Collective’s ongoing evolution and innovation as a business,” David Thomas, CEO of Brand Collective said.
Hilco Capital placed Cue Clothing Co into administration and receivership almost one month ago. At the start of the receivership process, the retailer lost five stores from its network.
Source: Inside Retail Australia (https://insideretail.com.au/business/financial/formal-offers-tabled-for-sunken-cue-clothing-co-202610)

item.title: Ad tech firms see 11.7% of ad impressions hit by Apple’s Safari tracking block
item.description:
Aditude reported that Safari on iPhones and iPads accounts for 11.7% of the ads its customers show and 11.4% of their ad revenue, while eCPMs fell 10.5% among readers who installed Apple’s latest software update. Only about 8% of users have upgraded to the update so far, but Aditude estimates the overall revenue impact at roughly 1% at this stage.
Publishers that rely heavily on programmatic advertising in Safari have seen little immediate effect, according to consultant Scott Messer, who notes that impact may grow as more users install the update. Some senior commercial executives at news publishers told Digiday they have not yet observed any impact, citing subscription‑heavy business models that reduce dependence on Safari‑based ads. Others warn that the block could hurt publishers with low direct‑sold inventory more than brands that monetize a large share through direct‑sold campaigns, and that vendors landing on Apple’s restriction list would exacerbate losses. Ad industry executives said they have been on edge since the unannounced change, noting that Apple’s lack of transparency makes it difficult to anticipate which tracking partners will be affected.
“The trend has definitely been more restrictive for anything that generates an identifier, specifically on Apple. It’s not going to get better. I would say it’s going to get worse,” Davide Rosamilia' said.
Apple’s earlier crackdowns on tracking in 2017 and 2021 wiped billions off the online ad industry, with Meta saying the 2021 change would cost it around $10 billion in a single year. Those precedents have left advertisers wary of further restrictions on identifier‑based targeting. The latest Safari update arrived without warning and uses a non‑public list to block major tracking firms.
Source: Digiday (https://digiday.com/media/ad-industry-tallies-early-losses-from-apples-safari-tracking-block)

item.title: SurfStitch shifts to lifestyle marketplace after 10‑month restructure
item.description:
SurfStitch has relaunched as a pure‑play marketplace focused on Australian coastal culture after a 10‑month restructuring led by Olvera Advisors. The platform now serves about 1.7 million customers and features roughly 75 predominantly Australian brands.
Under the new marketplace model, brands set their own discounts but agree not to use SurfStitch as a dumping ground for excess inventory, and outside specified promotional periods core ranges must be sold at full price or at levels comparable to the brands’ own websites. SurfStitch avoids placing all of its approximately 75 brands on sale simultaneously, aiming to prevent the site from becoming a digital flea market. To give shoppers a reason to return, the Guides hub offers a Surf Guide scoring 100 Australian beaches daily, a Hikes Guide detailing trails, and a Gig Guide covering music and festivals at coastal venues.
“We are moving SurfStitch into more of a trusted lifestyle platform that happens to sell product,” Damien Hodgkinson, principal at Olvera Advisors and lead on the restructuring and platform redesign said.
“We don’t want SurfStitch to be a digital flea market. It will have a strong editorial and visual point of view,” Damien Hodgkinson, principal at Olvera Advisors said.
In March 2025, Best Markets Group acquired SurfStitch from Alquemie Group with plans to reposition the business. When it could not reach an agreement with its landlord and a supplier to withdraw a winding-up petition, Olvera was appointed to undertake a formal restructuring through voluntary administration.
Source: Inside Retail Australia (https://insideretail.com.au/business/from-discount-trap-to-lifestyle-platform-inside-the-surfstitch-restructure-202610)

item.title: Australian businesses add ‘service fees’ after Oct 1 card surcharge ban
item.description:
Australian businesses began adding ‘service fees’ to customer bills after the card surcharge ban took effect on October 1. The Reserve Bank estimates that consumers paid about $1.6 billion in card surcharges during the 2024-25 fiscal year.
The ban, enforced by Visa, Mastercard, Eftpos and American Express, prohibits merchants from adding a separate charge for card payments, though genuine service or booking fees unrelated to payment method remain allowed. The ACCC warns that relabelling a card surcharge as a ‘service fee’ may constitute misleading conduct if the charge is triggered solely by using a card. Businesses may absorb the card‑processing fees, negotiate cheaper rates with payment providers, or incorporate the costs into the base price of goods and services. Some cafes and restaurants have responded by raising menu prices on October 1 to cover ongoing expenses, potentially shifting the burden to cash‑paying shoppers unless a discount for alternative payments is disclosed.
Before October 1, merchants could add a surcharge to card transactions, a practice the Reserve Bank said applied to about 16% of businesses and generated roughly $1.6 billion in annual consumer payments. The Reserve Bank’s guidance now bars Visa, Mastercard, Eftpos and American Express from permitting such surcharges, aiming to eliminate hidden card‑payment costs. Although large retailers generally did not apply surcharges, many small cafes, grocers and online stores relied on the fee to offset card‑acceptance expenses.
Source: Inside Retail Australia (https://insideretail.com.au/business/new-service-fees-appear-after-card-surcharge-ban-are-they-legal-202610)

item.title: UK retail footfall drops 2.9% in September as shopping centre visits slide 3.5%
item.description:
UK retail footfall fell 2.9% in September 2026 compared with September 2025, according to BRC‑Sensormatic data. Shopping centre visits declined 3.5% year on year, while retail park traffic slipped 1.7% and high street footfall fell 3% Northern Ireland was the only UK nation to record growth, with visits rising 2.1%
In England footfall dropped 3.4%, in Wales it fell 3% and in Scotland it decreased 0.7% over the same period. The British Retail Consortium urged the government to cut business costs via the forthcoming Autumn Budget, calling for relief on business rates to help retailers invest, keep prices competitive and support jobs. Sensormatic’s head of consulting for Europe, the Middle East and Africa, Andy Sumpter, said inflation, household budget pressure, fuel costs and Budget uncertainty drove the September decline. The BRC‑Sensormatic monitor tracks visits to retail destinations as a proxy for shopper activity rather than actual sales.
“She argued that relief would help retailers invest in stores, keep prices competitive and support jobs as businesses prepare for Christmas,” Helen Dickinson, BRC chief executive said.
“He pointed instead to inflation, pressure on household budgets, fuel costs and uncertainty ahead of the Budget as factors influencing shopper behaviour,” Andy Sumpter, Sensormatic’s head of consulting and analytics for Europe, the Middle East and Africa said.
In August 2026, UK retail footfall declined 1.7% year on year, shopping centre visits slipped 0.5% and retail park visits grew 1%. High street footfall was down 3.1% in August.
Source: Retail Insight Network (https://retail-insight-network.com/news/uk-retail-footfall-falls-2-9-as-shopping-centre-visits-decline)

item.title: Ramp reaches $60 billion valuation after $1.85 billion funding round
item.description:
Ramp announced a new funding round on Friday, Oct. 9, raising $1.85 billion and achieving a $60 billion valuation. The $60 billion valuation excludes the fresh capital, making Ramp the most highly valued private company in corporate spend management.
The round follows a Series F in June that brought in $750 million at a $44 billion valuation. Ramp said it now serves 70,000 businesses, up from 50,000 at the start of 2026, and that its annualized revenue had topped $1.5 billion. Its closest rival, Brex, was sold to Capital One earlier this year for $5 billion. Ramp also highlighted its Router tool, which it said reduces AI costs by about 30% by selecting the optimal model for each task.
“finance is going through the biggest structural change since the spreadsheet,” Eric Glyman, Co-Founder and CEO said.
In September, Bloomberg reported that Ramp was in early talks for a $60 billion valuation. That followed the company’s Series F in June, which raised $750 million at a $44 billion valuation. Earlier in 2026, Brex was acquired by Capital One for $5 billion.
Source: PYMNTS (https://pymnts.com/news/investment-tracker/fintech-investments/2026/ramp-valued-at-60-billion-following-new-funding-round)

item.title: Fed Data Shows 20% of U.S. Households Fell Behind on Loan Payments
item.description:
The Federal Reserve’s Survey of Consumer Finances, released on October 9, found that nearly 20% of U.S. families were behind on loan payments in 2025, up from about 12% in the 2022 survey. The survey also showed the poorest quarter of households losing more than half of their net worth, falling from $3,800 to $1,700. Median wealth for Black families dropped 25% after a 60% gain in the 2022 survey.
Households using buy now, pay later services increased from 7% in the 2022 survey to 12% in the latest 2025 data, according to the Fed’s Survey of Consumer Finances. The survey covered the 2022‑2025 period, during which annual GDP growth averaged about 2.5% and the consumer‑price index rose 3.6% per year on average. While incomes rose for less‑well‑off Americans over the same timeframe, their net worth did not increase, leaving the poorest quarter of households with $1,700 in wealth compared with $3,800 in 2022. Consumers facing high financial stress were 6 percentage points more likely to have made their most recent grocery purchase online than those with low stress, with 16% versus 10% reporting online grocery purchases.
In the 2022 Survey of Consumer Finances, about 12% of families reported being behind on loan payments and 7% used buy now, pay later services. Median wealth for Black families had risen 60% in the 2022 survey before the latest decline. The survey’s release date was Friday, October 9, as noted in the Fed’s announcement.
Source: PYMNTS (https://pymnts.com/consumer-finance/2026/20-of-americans-behind-on-loans-fed-data-shows)

item.title: Meta sued over ‘Ends today’ AI glasses emails that kept $224 sale live
item.description:
Meta is facing a proposed class action after a May 25 email titled “Ends today: AI glasses from $224” advertised a deadline that never arrived. Two weeks later the company’s site was still offering the glasses at $224, and an audit found that price available for 33 consecutive days.
The email promised up to 25% off the glasses, which were listed as 25% off a $299 regular price. Camilleri alleges that the “Ends today” and “Last‑chance” messages violate Washington’s Commercial Electronic Mail Act and Consumer Protection Act. He seeks to represent all Washington residents who received the promotional emails and is requesting $100 in statutory damages for each email sent.
Source: Shopifreaks (https://shopifreaks.com/meta-faces-a-class-action-claiming-its-ends-today-ai-glasses-emails-broke-washington-law-because-the-224-sale-kept-running)

item.title: Orlando trucking owner pleads guilty to $1 million USPS freight‑auction fraud
item.description:
Khayyam Arif Oglu Farajov, the Orlando‑based owner of Talishco LLC, pleaded guilty on Friday to one wire‑fraud count and one money‑laundering count in a scheme that collected more than $1 million. He agreed to forfeit the seized brokerage accounts and pay $993,979 in restitution, while each conviction carries a maximum federal prison sentence of 20 years.
Farajov enrolled Talishco in the USPS Freight Auction program in May 2022 and, between June 2022 and January 2023, won hundreds of contracts for bulk‑mail transportation. He repeatedly failed to send trucks for the routes he secured, offered excuses about missing drivers, and later falsely marked those shipments as delivered to trigger payments. The proceeds were moved through accounts linked to shell companies under his control and then invested in the stock market for personal enrichment. Federal investigators traced the funds, seized the two brokerage accounts, and the USPS Office of Inspector General led the investigation. USPS requires proof of delivery before paying Freight Auction suppliers, accepting tracking scans, electronic messages or manual submissions through its Logistics Gateway. However, the 2024 federal audit found that the agency did not properly verify those records before issuing payments.
The USPS launched the Freight Auction program in October 2021 to secure trucking capacity through competitive spot‑market bidding. A 2024 federal audit identified 102 participating transportation suppliers during fiscal years 2022 and 2023. The same audit found weaknesses in how the agency validated proof‑of‑delivery records, noting 69,225 paid trips worth about $197.9 million lacked reliable support.
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/orlando-trucking-owner-pleads-guilty-in-1m-usps-freight-auction-fraud)

item.title: Northwest freight rejections jump to 20.3% while Midwest holds steady at 18.6%
item.description:
FreightWaves data show the Northwest region’s tender rejection rate rose to 20.27% on Oct. 8, more than triple its level a year earlier. The Midwest followed at 18.61%, keeping the region above 15% since February, while other regions stayed between 7.6% and 13.1%. The Northwest surge is driven by a reefer‑focused harvest boom, whereas the Midwest’s tightness spans all equipment types.
In the Northwest, reefer rejections averaged about 41% in October, up from roughly 17% in July, while van rejections remained below 5% and reefer tender volume increased 65% since July and 35% versus a year ago. Van volume in the Northwest fell 11% compared with last year, reflecting a shift toward refrigerated loads for the apple and potato harvest in Washington, Oregon and Idaho. In the Midwest, van rejections hovered near 15% — about two and a half times the prior year’s level — and reefer rejections were near 29%, up from 15%, with overall tender volume up roughly 10% year over year, outpacing the 8% national gain. National tender rejections have eased to about 13.8% over the past two weeks, masking the regional divergence.
Before August, the Northwest was one of the loosest regions in the country, with rejection rates between 6% and 9% from January through July. The Midwest had been the tightest large region for most of 2026, maintaining rejection rates near or above 15% since February. Nationally, tender rejections have eased to about 13.8% over the past two weeks. The pattern mirrors last year’s harvest, though the 2026 spike arrived earlier and reached higher levels.
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/the-two-tightest-regions-tell-two-very-different-stories-about-the-freight-market)

item.title: Nat Habit raises ₹142 Cr to expand offline reach to 200,000 stores
item.description:
Nat Habit has secured ₹142 Cr (around $14.7 million) in a Series C funding round led by Trident Growth Partners. The capital will be used to grow its offline footprint from roughly 20,000 stores to 200,000 stores over the next three years.
The fresh capital will be deployed to invest in research and development, formulation, and new manufacturing facilities for the planned sunscreen and serum lines. Nat Habit intends to strengthen its presence on quick‑commerce platforms alongside the offline rollout. The brand will also adjust pack sizes and communication to target what it calls the ‘Bharat consumer’, expanding beyond its current higher‑income, higher‑education base. Existing investors Bertelsmann India Investments, Mirabilis Investment Trust, and Sharrp Ventures participated in the round, while Physis Capital and Hero Family Office joined the cap table. Nat Habit reports having served more than 60 lakh households across India and cites an annualised gross revenue of ₹330 crore. Before this Series C, the startup raised $10.2 million in a Series B round in 2023, which it said would fund product diversification, brand building, offline expansion and hiring.
“Our ambition now is to make our products accessible to many more households across India,” Swagatika Das, cofounder said.
Before this round, Nat Habit raised $10.2 million in its Series B funding in 2023 for product diversification, brand building, offline expansion and hiring. The fundraise adds to recent investments in India’s ayurvedic and herbal wellness segment, following Kapiva’s $60 million Series D in September 2025 and its ₹50 crore innovation fund launched earlier this year.
Source: Inc42 (https://inc42.com/buzz/d2c-brand-nat-habit-raises-%E2%82%B9142-cr-to-scale-offline-expansion)

item.title: Online auction sells 171 antique glass eyes for $2,640
item.description:
Potter & Potter sold a drawer of 171 antique prosthetic glass eyes for $2,640 at its Oct. 1 auction. The lot attracted 11 bids and the price includes the buyer’s premium.
The eyes are early 20th‑century German prosthetic glass eyes, arranged in a wooden grid drawer. A condition report noted light dust and occasionally sharp glass ends. Shipping expenses for the lot include labor, materials, insurance and transportation. Potter & Potter’s conditions of sale cover the purchase price, buyer’s premium, applicable taxes and other charges.
The auction was part of Potter & Potter’s “Weird Tales! UFOs, Curiosities and Tattoos” sale, which offered 569 lots. Online access gave shoppers an opportunity to browse a collection that would make an ordinary estate sale look positively restrained.
Source: PYMNTS (https://pymnts.com/pymnts-features/the-weekender/2026/online-auctions-put-a-price-on-strange)

item.title: Indian startups raise $122.9 million in first week of October
item.description:
Indian startups raised $122.9 million across 25 deals between October 5 and October 9, according to Inc42. The amount marks a 47.4% decline from the $233.6 million raised in 16 deals the prior week. Ecommerce led the sector with $63.9 million across nine deals, driven by DailyObjects’ $34.3 million Series C.
Fintech secured $24 million, advanced hardware and technology attracted $10 million, while edtech and healthtech each brought in roughly $9 million and $8 million respectively, with fintech led by BITKRAFT Ventures in StockGro’s round.
The previous week saw startups raise $233.6 million across 16 deals. This week’s figures cover the period October 5 through October 9.
Source: Inc42 (https://inc42.com/buzz/from-dailyobjects-to-stockgro-indian-startups-raised-about-123-mn-this-week)

item.title: Revolut aims to match biggest U.S. tech firms after $115B valuation
item.description:
On Oct. 9, Revolut CEO Nik Storonsky said the company, valued at $115 billion, aims to expand its technology suite and eventually rival the largest U.S. tech firms. He pointed to a proprietary AI model called PRAGMA, trained on 40 billion transactions from 25 million users across 111 countries, as the foundation for future products.
Revolut processes roughly 30 to 40 million transactions each day, giving it a large data set for training its models. The company received conditional OCC approval for a U.S. national bank charter on Sept. 3. It is working with the FDIC and Federal Reserve to complete remaining requirements. On Sept. 16 Revolut added a banking license in Colombia, bringing its total of full banking licenses worldwide to six.
“With 30 to 40 million transactions taking place every day on Revolut, we have a unique dataset to build on,” Nik Storonsky, CEO said.
Before these announcements, Revolut had already secured bank licenses in the United Kingdom, France, Australia, Lithuania and Mexico. The company had been pursuing a U.S. banking charter to enable credit cards and loans in America.
Source: PYMNTS (https://pymnts.com/business/2026/revolut-ceo-targets-long-term-growth-with-proprietary-models)

item.title: Google pilots Local Coupons for retailers, charging only on redemption
item.description:
Google has begun a pilot of Local Coupons, a Search ads offering that displays discounts to nearby shoppers and stores the coupon in their mobile wallet for in-store use. Retailers are charged only when a shopper actually redeems the coupon at checkout, linking the ad directly to an in-store sale. Each coupon carries a unique code that the register verifies at scan time to prevent double redemption.
Google has not disclosed which retailers are participating in the pilot or when it might expand the program more widely. The service aims to give advertisers a measurable connection between online search activity and physical store purchases.
Source: Shopifreaks (https://shopifreaks.com/google-pilots-local-coupons-which-put-store-deals-in-search-and-mobile-wallets-and-only-charge-retailers-when-shoppers-redeem)

item.title: Beximco seeks approval to reopen factories with foreign investment
item.description:
Beximco Group is seeking government approval for a new leasing model to partially reopen more than a dozen shuttered apparel and textile factories at its Gazipur park with backing from British firm Charter HCP and Chinese company Besting. If approved, the first factory could resume operations in April next year, with jackets for export making up about 90 percent of its output.
The factory would initially employ around 2,500 workers. Under the proposed arrangement, loan repayments would be sourced from the factory’s export proceeds. If the model succeeds, Beximco says it could reopen the remaining closed units in phases, potentially restoring jobs for many former employees.
“they hope to partially restart Prefix Fashions under the proposed leasing arrangement,” Khalid Shahrior, senior general manager of Beximco’s Textiles & Apparel Division, and Huda Mohammed Faisal, CEO of Revival Global said.
Beximco once ranked as one of Bangladesh’s largest private sector employers before its empire collapsed following the fall of the Awami League government and the arrest of co‑founder Salman F. Rahman. The shutdown of its garment units left workers without jobs.
Source: Sourcing Journal (https://wwd.com/sourcing-journal/sustainability/on-the-line-beximco-india-protests-colombia-albania-1239336284)

item.title: Billion Rise opens $100 million high‑tech factory in Vietnam
item.description:
Billion Rise has opened a new high‑tech factory in Thanh Hoa, Vietnam, backed by a $100 million investment. The facility spans approximately 320,000 square meters and is slated to produce up to 100 million meters of fabric each year.
The factory is being built in three phases, with the first phase of about 110,000 square meters already complete as of now. Additional knitting, dyeing and printing capacity will be added in the second phase, scheduled for finish in the third quarter of next year, as expected. The final phase is set for completion in the third quarter of 2029, bringing overall warp and weft knitting, dyeing, digital, flat‑bed and heat‑transfer printing, stentering and finishing, plus a wastewater treatment system and solar rooftop. The factory also includes an advanced wastewater treatment system and solar rooftop to help minimize its environmental footprint.
“With our new factory, we can now better support brands looking to build more integrated value chains in Vietnam while expanding our business across these important markets,” Steven Moore, global sales director at Billion Rise said.
Billion Rise is a Hong Kong‑based vertically integrated apparel and textile company. The company already operates a manufacturing base in Qing Yuan, China and has spent a decade investing in Vietnam to match the standards of its Chinese facility.
Source: Sourcing Journal (https://wwd.com/sourcing-journal/industry-news/billion-rise-opens-apparel-factory-in-vietnam-1239335615)

item.title: Shopify adds weekly auto-sync for up to eight languages in EU stores
item.description:
Shopify now provides automatic weekly translation updates for up to eight languages to merchants in Austria, Belgium, Denmark, France, Germany, Ireland, Italy, Netherlands, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom. Previously, Shopify supported only two languages and required merchants to manually re‑translate content after each edit.
Merchants can enable Auto‑sync for any published language by opening Translate & Adapt, selecting the language, and toggling the Auto‑sync switch. Once enabled, Shopify scans the store each week and translates any new or updated product descriptions, collection pages, or other store content into the selected language. Translations that merchants have entered manually are protected and will never be overwritten by the automatic process. The former Auto‑translate button has been renamed ‘Translate now’ for on‑demand translations, and using either Auto‑sync or Translate now consumes one of the eight language slots available per store. You can turn Auto‑sync on or off for each language at any time, giving merchants full control over which languages receive automatic updates. Auto‑sync is disabled by default and must be activated per language via the toggle in Translate & Adapt.
Until now, editing a product description or any other store content meant going back into the app to re‑translate it yourself. As a result, translated storefronts fell behind and buyers landed on outdated content in their language. As usual, translations you wrote manually are never overwritten.
Source: Shopify Changelog (https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/translate-adapt-auto-sync-translations-for-up-to-8-languages)

item.title: Lycra showcases 70% plant-based renewable fiber at Textile Exchange Conference
item.description:
The Lycra Company will showcase a renewable fiber made from field corn at the Textile Exchange Conference in Vancouver from October 12 to 16. The fiber contains 70 percent plant-based content and can cut its carbon footprint by up to 45 percent compared with petroleum-based spandex.
The renewable fiber uses U.S.-grown dent corn as a key feedstock, sourced largely from Iowa, and is now produced at commercial scale.
“Bringing more recycled and renewable materials to commercial scale is essential to turning the industry’s ambitions into action,” Alistair Williamson, company vice president of product sustainability said.
Over the last few years, Lycra said it has been working with textile recyclers worldwide to build and refine systems that separate spandex from companion yarns, such as nylon and polyester, from pre-consumer textile waste, and spin it back into new spandex fibers.
Source: Sourcing Journal (https://wwd.com/sourcing-journal/industry-news/lycra-textile-exchange-conference-renewable-corn-1239336088)

item.title: Contract truckload rates climb to 52-week high of $2.72 per mile plus fuel
item.description:
FreightWaves SONAR data showed contract truckload rates reaching a 52-week high of $2.72 per mile plus fuel, up 18% year over year, as of an Oct. 9 market update. Spot rates tracked by the NTI index rose nearly 50% year over year, while the Outbound Tender Reject Index held at 13.75% and weekly truckload demand increased about 1.25%.
Tender rejections stayed within the recent 13%-14% band, indicating range-bound but elevated pressure on carriers to accept loads. A Gulf-coast storm identified as Isaías caused localized spikes in rejections and spot rates in the Mobile and Montgomery, Alabama markets. FreightWaves also added intermodal rate benchmarks to its SONAR Rate Intelligence module, letting users compare lanes, nearby rail ramps and cost savings versus van for both contract and spot shipments.
Before the October update, contract rates had retreated from earlier highs following a brief post-Labor Day pullback in truckload demand. The Outbound Tender Reject Index had been fluctuating inside a 13%-14% range, and spot rates had shown moderate year-over-year gains. Carriers and shippers were beginning to reset agreements as annual bidding cycles approached.
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/trucking-rates-spike-contracts-at-52-week-high)

item.title: Mastercard CEO says stablecoins can solve cross-border payment delays
item.description:
In an interview with Bloomberg TV, Mastercard CEO Michael Miebach said stablecoins offer an instant alternative to cross-border payments that currently take days and have unclear fees. Open Standard announced on September 30 that its U.S. dollar-backed OUSD stablecoin is live, with Mastercard among four integration options alongside Stripe, Coinbase, and Visa.
On June 30, Open Standard said the stablecoin would launch later in 2026 and noted that several dozen companies had signed up, calling OUSD a money movement stablecoin.
“From a working capital perspective for a company, if you could move the money instantly, it would be so much better,” Michael Miebach, CEO, Mastercard said.
“For issuers with international reach, these two use cases together make B2B cross-border infrastructure one of the clearest near-term growth opportunities,” PYMNTS Intelligence report said.
Earlier in June, Open Standard said its stablecoin would launch later in 2026 and noted that several dozen firms had already signed up to use it.
Source: PYMNTS (https://pymnts.com/news/cross-border-payments/2026/mastercard-ceo-says-stablecoins-solve-cross-border-payment-delays)

item.title: GreyOrange acquires Site Bionics to add digital twin tech to gStore
item.description:
GreyOrange has acquired Site Bionics, the developer of an AI-powered digital twin platform. The acquisition lets retailers turn existing security cameras into a live, continuously updated model of store activity.
The technology will be integrated first with gStore, GreyOrange’s AI-powered retail SaaS for store inventory and omnichannel operations. It combines Site Bionics’ video‑language models with gStore’s item‑level RFID intelligence to give a single AI‑driven view of products and people on the floor. All processing happens on‑site, tracking is anonymous, and the system is protected by enterprise‑grade security and privacy controls.
“For years, this industry has promised retailers that RFID and computer vision would come together and show them the full story of their stores. That promise has gone unmet,” Adam Blair, co‑founder of Site Bionics said.
Site Bionics was founded by Adam Blair, former chief technology officer of Radar, and Don Gillett, former head architect of Amazon Go. GreyOrange says the Site Bionics team will deploy the technology in gStore first, with plans to extend it to warehouse operations through the GreyMatter platform.
Source: Sourcing Journal (https://wwd.com/sourcing-journal/industry-news/greyorange-acquires-site-bionics-1239333572)

item.title: Stord secures $400 million credit facility led by Citi and names new CFO, CRO
item.description:
Stord closed a $400 million credit facility led by Citi on Thursday and appointed Bill Zerella as chief financial officer and Mark Wayland as chief revenue officer. The facility was oversubscribed, closing at nearly double its original target size.
The credit facility follows a $250 million Series F round led by Strike Capital in May that valued Stord at $3 billion. Combined, the equity and credit capacity now totals $650 million for 2026, according to the company. Stord operates nearly 100 fulfillment locations worldwide, serves over 1,000 brands, and processes more than $15 billion in gross merchandise volume each year.
“This facility, combined with our $250 million Series F, gives us the balance sheet to match the scale, potential, and impact of what we’re building,” Sean Henry, CEO and co-founder of Stord said.
The deal follows a $250 million Series F led by Strike Capital in May that valued Stord at $3 billion. Stord has expanded its footprint through acquisitions including ProPack Logistics and Pitney Bowes’ e‑commerce fulfillment unit in 2024, Ware2Go from UPS in May 2025, and Shipwire from Ceva Logistics in January.
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/stord-400m-credit-facility-citi)

item.title: Adrian Jules launches tech platform for luxury custom tailors
item.description:
Adrian Jules Custom Clothier, founded in 1964 in Rochester, New York, is drawing on its 62‑year tailoring heritage to roll out a technology platform for private‑label retailers. The company’s internally built ERP system now powers a client‑facing portal that shows real‑time fabric availability, pricing and high‑resolution images from suppliers in Europe, South America and Asia. To ensure consistent fit regardless of garment type or production location, the platform standardizes measurement specifications for suits, knits, polos and jackets.
Over three generations the business has expanded its retail outlets and increased its American manufacturing capacity. The ERP system tracks each garment from order entry through workshop cutting, construction and accounting. Clients can place orders online via the proprietary portal, which also speeds up pattern introductions and production‑throughput tracking. The technology‑enabled offering is marketed under the Adrian Jules Platinum line, which integrates custom apparel production across global supply chains.
“Technology has been a gamechanger for us,” Arnie Roberti, president of operations said.
The company was established in Rochester, New York, in 1964 by an Italian designer and master tailor who had come to the United States from Italy. Across three generations the business has expanded the number of its retail outlets and has increased its American manufacturing capacity.
Source: WWD (https://wwd.com/sourcing-journal/industry-news/where-60-years-of-master-craftsmanship-meets-modern-luxury-1239333081)

item.title: Kodiak and Charger launch autonomous trucks on 435‑mile Dallas‑Laredo route
item.description:
Kodiak AI and Charger Logistics launched autonomous freight service on a 435‑mile lane between Dallas and Laredo, Texas, as announced Thursday. Kodiak’s long‑haul Autonomy Readiness Measure reached 96% at the end of September, up from 93% in August and 84% in February.
A safety driver remains behind the wheel for now, with the companies planning to shift to driverless operations once Kodiak completes its safety case. The inaugural run occurred on September 8, moving refrigerated and dry van freight for consumer‑packaged‑goods and food‑and‑beverage shippers between Charger’s Dallas and Laredo terminals. Laredo, the nation’s highest‑volume commercial land port, processed over $350 billion of international trade in 2025, and the lane marks Kodiak’s first autonomous route serving that gateway.
“Autonomy lets us build a network that serves both our customers and our drivers,” Andy Khera, president of Charger Logistics said.
“Charger came to us knowing what they wanted from autonomy and what they need to see before scaling it,” Don Burnette, founder and CEO of Kodiak said.
Before this launch, Kodiak’s driverless trucks had been operating in commercial service in the Permian Basin since December 2024. Charger also has an autonomous trucking agreement with Aurora Innovation for second‑generation driverless trucks on the same Dallas‑Laredo lane, a deal reported in August. Kodiak’s readiness metric had risen from 84% in February to 93% in August before reaching 96% at the end of September.
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/kodiak-charger-autonomous-trucks-dallas-laredo)

item.title: E.l.f. Brands rolls out $13 fragrance mist and body cream line
item.description:
E.l.f. Brands announced on Monday that it has entered the fragrance and body care categories with a limited-edition collection called E.l.f. Pop. The fragrance mist and body cream retail for $13, while a travel-size kit costs $12.
The debut collection, dubbed Spicy Bundt Nice, features notes of holiday spice cake, orange zest, cardamom, butter cream frosting, cedarwood and musk. Products are vegan and cruelty free. Additional E.l.f. Pop scents are slated for release in January.
“Fragrance is a unique form of self-expression; it is personal and customizable. Body care transforms an everyday necessity into a ritual of self-care and indulgence,” Oshiya Savur, chief marketing officer at E.l.f. Brands said.
Source: Retail Dive (https://retaildive.com/news/elf-brands-fragrance-athleta-ceo-lululemon-crocs-bark/832592)

item.title: Port of Mobile stops operations as Hurricane Isaias brings 120 mph winds
item.description:
The Port of Mobile ceased vessel traffic and cargo handling on Oct. 9 after the Alabama Port Authority announced a shutdown ahead of Hurricane Isaias. The U.S. Coast Guard set Port Condition ZULU, warning gale-force winds within 12 hours, and cargo work is suspended except for Coast Guard-authorized activities.
The port's single container terminal, run by APM Terminals, normally moves about 600,000 TEUs each year and can handle up to 2.5 million TEUs at full gateway capacity. Its AutoMobile International Terminal processes roll-on/roll-off vehicles, with space for 150,000 cars yearly, 7,000 on-site storage slots and a 40,000-square-foot inspection center. Before the shutdown, workers secured cranes, cargo and equipment to protect them from the storm's impact.
The Port of Mobile's container, general cargo and bulk facilities sit near five Class I railroads, four short-line lines and almost 15,000 miles of inland waterways, according to the port's website. Before the closure, workers secured cranes, cargo and equipment to safeguard them from the approaching Category 3 storm.
Source: Supply Chain Dive (https://supplychaindive.com/news/port-of-mobile-shutters-operations-ahead-of-hurricane-isaias/832621)

item.title: EU plans new surveillance fee on non‑EU parcels alongside existing charges
item.description:
The European Commission is developing a new surveillance fee for packages entering the EU from outside the bloc, to be added to the current 3‑euro import duty and the forthcoming 2‑euro customs handling charge. The fee, described in a leaked draft of the European Product Act as the “Union market surveillance fee,” is intended to fund market surveillance and could trigger fines of up to 6 % of a company’s global annual revenue.
As of 1 July this year, a flat import fee of 3 euros per product category in a parcel has been in effect, and it will be superseded by standard customs duties starting in July 2028. From 1 November, a separate handling fee of 2 euros per declaration line is expected to be introduced, without any VAT component. The surveillance fee would be levied on importers, with the liability for direct shipments from online retailers still to be determined, and would be lower for bulk imports than for individual consumer shipments.
For years, Brussels has watched with concern as packages from online retailers—particularly those from China—have flooded the European Union. In its latest annual report, the agency identified this lack of oversight as a top risk. This handling fee is intended to strengthen inspection of ecommerce shipments.
Source: Ecommerce News Netherlands (https://ecommercenews.nl/brussel-werkt-aan-nog-een-pakketheffing)

item.title: ASOS and adidas launch Collection 05 with four‑day Paris pop‑up
item.description:
ASOS and adidas Originals opened a four‑day pop‑up for Collection 05 at the adidas Champs‑Élysées store, running from 16 to 19 October. The pop‑up sold out all core styles, marking it as one of the store’s most successful activations to date.
The collection became available to ASOS.World loyalty members on 15 October and launched globally on 16 October, coinciding with the pop‑up’s opening day at the Champs‑Élysées store. It follows a previous pop‑up that ASOS and adidas held at the adidas flagship store on Oxford Street earlier in the year. Inspired by 80s maximalist sports nostalgia, Collection 05 reinterprets the confidence, attitude and expressive styling of that era through a contemporary fashion lens, using leather, sheened nylon and satin in a palette of black, deep brown, neutrals and rust with blue, yellow and orange accents. Core pieces highlighted in the launch include a cut‑and‑sew overhead track jacket in rust, an embellished check track jacket in brown co‑ord and a tailored track jacket in grey marl co‑ord.
“For Collection 05, we wanted to give people the confidence to be bolder with sportswear. We’ve pushed the contrast between sport and glamour through exaggerated proportions, rich textures and unexpected details, creating pieces with attitude that everyone can style and make their own,” Vanessa Spence, executive vice president, brand and creative at ASOS said.
ASOS and adidas Originals have launched their latest collaboration, Collection 05. It follows a previous pop‑up that the brands held at adidas’ Oxford Street flagship store.
Source: Retail Gazette (https://retailgazette.co.uk/blog/2026/10/asos-adidas-paris)

item.title: Block launches ad campaign targeting 60 million bitcoin‑curious Americans
item.description:
Block launched a consumer advertising campaign last week aimed at 60 million bitcoin‑curious Americans The move follows Block’s October 2025 integration of bitcoin payments into Square point‑of‑sale terminals and its 5% discount for Cash App users who spend bitcoin at Square merchants
Cash App reports about 59 million active wallet users, while Square’s platform hosts roughly 4 million sellers. Since launching bitcoin sales on Cash App in January 2018, Block says about 24 million consumers have purchased the cryptocurrency through the app. The October 2025 update lets Square merchants accept bitcoin payments and optionally convert a portion of card sales into bitcoin. Block’s 5% bitcoin discount applies when Cash App users pay with the cryptocurrency at a participating Square merchant.
“I don’t think anybody else has an opportunity to kick off a two-sided marketplace like this,” Miles Suter, head of bitcoin and stablecoin at Block said.
“I don’t think there is anything more important in my lifetime to work on,” Jack Dorsey, founder of Block said.
Block introduced bitcoin sales on Cash App in January 2018, which has since attracted about 24 million active purchasers. In October 2025 the company integrated bitcoin payments into Square point‑of‑sale terminals, allowing merchants to accept and convert card sales to bitcoin.
Source: Payments Dive (https://paymentsdive.com/news/block-envisions-bitcoin-for-all/832610)

item.title: Walmart opens fifth automated fulfillment center in Stockton, California
item.description:
Walmart has opened its fifth high-tech fulfillment center, a 900,000-square-foot facility in Stockton, California, to increase online order processing and improve West Coast delivery times. The site uses a high-density storage and retrieval system that condenses the traditional 12-step fulfillment process into five steps. E-commerce now accounts for 23% of Walmart’s total sales, and the retailer says faster delivery helps drive more online purchases.
Walmart Fulfillment Services will also operate the center to handle orders placed by third-party sellers on its Marketplace platform. Located in California’s Central Valley, the facility places inventory closer to West Coast shoppers, enabling quicker shipping options on millions of items while reducing strain on other fulfillment centers in the network. Walmart already runs four comparable next‑generation centers in Joliet, Illinois; McCordsville, Indiana; Greencastle, Pennsylvania; and Lancaster, Texas, which together support next‑day or two‑day delivery to 95% of the U.S. population. The company announced in August that it will build a sixth ultra‑modern hub in Carnesville, Georgia, covering 1.5 million square feet, with construction slated to begin later this year and a total investment of $1.3 billion.
Before the Stockton opening, Walmart operated four next‑generation fulfillment centers in the Midwest and East Coast, aiming to reach 95% of Americans with next‑day or two‑day shipping. The retailer reported that e‑commerce sales made up 23% of its total revenue, highlighting the importance of speedy fulfillment for its online growth.
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/walmart-activates-automated-e-commerce-logistics-center-in-california)

item.title: eFormed Ventures buys 1898-founded Outdoor Life to launch AI gear marketplace
item.description:
eFormed Ventures acquired the 1898-founded hunting and camping magazine Outdoor Life from Recurrent Ventures. It plans to transform the title into an AI-driven outdoor gear marketplace that will sell products from outside retailers.
Outdoor Life currently earns revenue through affiliate links, but eFormed intends to operate its own store selling gear from external brands. The company will retain the magazine's editorial staff, whose product reviews and field tests will populate the marketplace. The platform will be powered by eFormed's proprietary AI system, Resonance 2.0, which recommends gear based on a shopper's location, season, browsing history, and past purchases. Resonance 2.0 aims to match users with products and prices tailored to their context.
Source: Shopifreaks (https://shopifreaks.com/eformed-ventures-acquires-outdoor-life-from-recurrent-ventures-to-turn-the-magazine-into-an-ai-powered-outdoor-gear-marketplace)

item.title: Paytm's lending revenue jumps to ₹2,594 Cr as payments growth slows
item.description:
In FY26, Paytm's financial services distribution reached ₹2,594 Cr, accounting for 31% of its ₹8,437 Cr topline, as the firm returned to profit with a net gain of ₹552 Cr. In Q1 FY27, operating revenue climbed 28% to ₹2,448 Cr and merchant GMV rose 31% to ₹7.1 lakh Cr, signalling continued momentum.
Payment services remained the largest segment at 58% of revenue, expanding at a 19% CAGR between FY21 and FY26. Paytm exited entertainment ticketing, scaled back e‑commerce ambitions and sharpened its focus on payments and financial services. Payment processing margins stayed above four basis points and subscription merchant deployments reached 1.57 crore storefronts. Paytm offsets the lack of UPI fees by offering merchant loans, insurance and point‑of‑sale device subscriptions. Paytm's super app approach now targets active payments users and merchants instead of chasing every consumer.
Paytm started as a digital wallet, expanded into a payments leader powered by UPI, and two years ago pivoted to lending after facing challenges with its payments bank. The move lifted Paytm to a net profit of ₹552 Cr in FY26, reversing a ₹663 Cr loss the prior year. Plans to introduce a 0.4% MDR fee on high‑value UPI transactions have been delayed, leaving the zero‑MDR framework in place.
Source: Inc42 (https://inc42.com/features/payments-vs-lending-the-tale-of-paytms-two-engines)

item.title: West Coast container rates slip $2 per FEU as trans-Pacific prices ease
item.description:
Far East‑U.S. West Coast spot rates fell $2 per FEU on Oct. 7, marking the first daily decline in weeks. Despite the drop, rates stayed 1.1% above their Sept. 30 level at $8,336 per FEU, while Asia‑U.S. East Coast averages rose to $11,512 per FEU, up 0.5% over the week. On the trans‑Atlantic lane, North Europe‑U.S. East Coast spot rates slipped 1.1% week over week to $2,854 per FEU.
Asia‑Mediterranean spot rates averaged $4,007 per FEU, down 5.9% from Sept. 30. Lower short‑term rates are giving European shippers more leverage as they negotiate long‑term contracts. The narrowing gap between Mediterranean and North Europe rates reflects shifting trade patterns.
“For European shippers, tender season is in full force and falling short-term rates are a welcome development as they negotiate long-term contracts,” Peter Sand, Chief Analyst at Xeneta said.
As demand eases from a high level, competition for vessel capacity is diminishing, improving negotiating conditions for shippers. Sand said carrier rerouting away from the Suez Canal route around Africa may help explain the pricing relationship.
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/us-west-coast-container-rates-edge-lower)

item.title: Boots adds OLAPLEX to 36 UK stores and online from 9 October
item.description:
Boots will stock OLAPLEX haircare in 36 of its UK stores and on boots.com starting 9 October, with the rollout finishing by November. The brand has become one of the most searched‑for premium haircare lines on Boots.com over the past three months among products not previously sold there.
Boots said it will add 50 new brands to its assortment ahead of the key holiday shopping period, as disclosed at its Christmas Showcase earlier this month. OLAPLEX’s offering at Boots will span its best‑selling treatments, wash‑care and styling products, all formulated with the brand’s patented bond‑building technology. The technology works at the molecular level to repair and strengthen hair from the inside out, aiming to improve look and feel while protecting against colour, heat and everyday damage. Both companies said the partnership will make OLAPLEX’s science‑backed approach to hair health available to a larger UK audience through stores and the boots.com website.
“We’re incredibly excited to welcome OLAPLEX to Boots. The level of consumer interest in the brand ahead of launch is clear, with OLAPLEX becoming one of the most searched-for premium haircare brands on Boots.com over the past three months, among brands not previously available at Boots,” Alice Rafferty, director of luxury beauty & cosmetics, Boots said.
“Boots is an incredibly exciting next step for OLAPLEX in the UK. We’ve always believed that everyone should have access to the science and innovation behind healthier-looking hair, and this partnership allows us to bring our patented bond technology to even more people,” Michelle Brett, chief revenue officer at OLAPLEX said.
OLAPLEX originated from a breakthrough in hair science and works at the molecular level to repair and strengthen damaged hair. The brand has built a global following by centering foundational hair health in its innovation, using patented bond technology.
Source: Retail Gazette (https://retailgazette.co.uk/blog/2026/10/boots-olaplex)

item.title: Truckload rates rise in 2026 as capacity exits market faster than freight
item.description:
Truckload rates rose in 2026 as carriers exited the market faster than freight demand grew. The average cost to operate a truck reached a record $2.336 per mile in 2025, according to ATRI’s Operational Costs of Trucking study. Spot linehaul rates remained below non‑fuel costs every year from 2023 through 2025, while contract linehaul gradually recovered.
Contract linehaul rates averaged $2.69 per mile in Q3 2026, still below Q4 2021 levels and having rebuilt only about half the profit cushion carriers enjoyed in 2022. Tolls rose 13.2%, repair and maintenance 8.6%, driver benefits 6.6% and tires 6.4%, setting records across nearly every cost line. Tender rejections have surged, with the STRI up 268% since October 2023 while tender volume rose only about 9%, and for‑hire tractor counts fell by roughly 51,000 in a single month. To cover overhead, rates would need to be about 14% higher than current benchmark levels, and even running near the hours‑of‑service ceiling a typical truck still falls about 5% short.
Carriers spent three years hauling at rates that barely covered their costs, often falling short in the spot market. The 2026 rate increase is described as a correction that is only about halfway done. In 2022, dry van contract linehaul averaged $2.81 per mile, but by 2024‑2025 it had fallen to $2.32 while non‑fuel costs rose roughly 30% from 2021 to 2025.
Source: FreightWaves (https://freightwaves.com/news/why-trucking-rates-are-rising-without-more-freight)

item.title: AAFA Urges USTR to Add Facebook, Instagram to 2026 Notorious Markets List
item.description:
The American Apparel and Footwear Association asked the Office of the United States Trade Representative to place Facebook, Instagram, Alibaba.com, AliExpress and DHGate on its 2026 Review of Notorious Markets for Counterfeiting and Piracy. The association said its recommendation reflects data from its membership of 1,100 brands and retailers across the fashion space.
Lamar said counterfeiters use online platforms to deceive consumers with fraudulent listings that mimic trusted brands and may contain hazardous chemicals. He added that a February 2025 study found 41 percent of 39 lab‑tested products failed international safety standards. AAFA noted that brands cannot police counterfeits alone and must constantly monitor marketplaces, a whack‑a‑mole effort many lack bandwidth for.
“Counterfeiters increasingly use online platforms to deceive consumers with fraudulent listings that mimic trusted brands to sell products that fail to meet basic safety standards and may contain hazardous chemicals or other dangerous substances,” Steve Lamar, president and CEO, AAFA said.
Commercial fraud and the sale of duped fashion products are on the rise, and the American Apparel and Footwear Association is urging the federal government to take action against online platforms it believes pose the greatest threat to the market. The proliferation of dupes and fakes across online platforms like Facebook and Instagram is undercutting U.S. fashion brands and endangering consumers, the group said.
Source: WWD (https://wwd.com/sourcing-journal/industry-news/aafa-meta-facebook-instagram-ustr-2026-notorious-markets-review-counterfeits-1239334279)

item.title: Federal court certifies class action for IEEPA tariff refunds
item.description:
The U.S. Court of International Trade certified a class of importers who paid IEEPA tariffs between Feb. 1, 2025 and Feb. 19, 2026, in a slip order issued Thursday. The court estimates that without class-action status, roughly $30 billion in IEEPA tariffs would remain with the government.
The certification covers importers who paid the tariffs during the specified period, excluding those who already filed individual lawsuits, and aims to provide a single refund pathway for all eligible entries. To date, more than 4,000 individual suits have been filed, and CBP has already refunded over $100 billion through its CAPE portal for the roughly $166 billion collected. The court also noted that CBP has begun processing refunds for finally liquidated entries this week, though only for a select group of importers with existing lawsuits.
“The decision doesn't immediately expand refund eligibility or direct payment,” James Kim said.
“It does, however, create a potential path forward for non-litigants, toward a single order requiring refunds to be issued to importers that have not pursued individual lawsuits,” James Kim said.
After the Supreme Court ruled the IEEPA tariffs illegal in February, the Court of International Trade ordered Customs and Border Protection to issue refunds for the approximately $166 billion collected. Since that order, CBP has distributed over $100 billion in refunds via the CAPE system and has recently expanded the portal to handle finally liquidated entries, albeit only for importers with active lawsuits. The Justice Department is appealing the refund order, arguing the court lacks authority to mandate reimbursements for importers who have not sued.
Source: Supply Chain Dive (https://supplychaindive.com/news/federal-court-clears-way-for-class-action-suit-against-ieepa-tariffs/832600)

item.title: NeoGrowth secures ₹85 crore to boost digital lending for Indian MSMEs
item.description:
NeoGrowth has raised ₹85 crore ($8.8 million) in a debt‑and‑equity round led by FMO with LeapFrog Investments participating. The proceeds will fund expansion of its digital lending platform, deepen market presence across India, and increase credit access for micro, small, and medium enterprises.
The platform manages nearly ₹2,000 crore in assets under management and has served more than 400,000 businesses to date.
NeoGrowth previously raised ₹300 crore in equity in 2022, with FMO contributing over half of that round. Existing backers include Omidyar Network, Lightrock, Khosla Impact, Accion Frontier Inclusion Fund–Quona Capital and 360 ONE Asset.
Source: Inc42 (https://inc42.com/buzz/neogrowth-raises-%E2%82%B985-cr-to-expand-digital-lending-capabilities)

item.title: Freemans launches multi‑million pound brand refresh targeting women over 40
item.description:
Freemans has launched a multi‑million pound brand refresh aimed at women over 40, a group that drives 93 per cent of household purchasing decisions according to the retailer. The retailer says women aged 40 spend £92 billion each year.
The refresh brings back the hand‑written signature last used in the 1950s, now appearing on packaging, email headers and promotional graphics. It introduces a colour palette of plums, greens and fluorescent accents for sales and special deals, replacing the mango‑toned logo previously used across the site and social media. Freemans notes the change follows a six‑year shift from paper catalogues to a fully digital platform, which included ending catalogue mailings and upgrading the website and mobile app. The updated website, deemed easier to shop by Drapers, will back a campaign across digital video, print, connected TV and nationwide radio using the slogan “Shopping is your department. And Freemans is your department store.” and radio spots with Chapman, Roslin, Ball and Thornton.
“While much of the retail sector is focused on attracting the next generation of shoppers, we’ve remained steadfast in our commitment to a customer we know exceptionally well: women over 40, one of the most influential consumer groups in the UK,” Ann Steer, CEO at Freemans said.
Over the past six years Freemans has moved from issuing catalogues to operating primarily online. The hand‑written signature had not appeared on the brand since the 1950s before its return in this refresh.
Source: Retail Gazette (https://retailgazette.co.uk/blog/2026/10/freemans-campaign)
